Data Phase: extraction, gate, and the recalibration pilot

All experimental points extracted this session from the scanned NTRS reports; all model numbers computed in the live NeuralFoil engine on kaanboge.github.io. Updated 2026-08-23 after the independent QC pass.

1 · Harris TM-81927, Figure 8 — NACA 0012 drag rise, four series 47 points holdout: never fitted

Machine gridline-calibrated extraction cross-checked by visual marker reading. Hollow markers = band-quality points where the printed curves merge (M 0.76–0.80, shaded). Stars at left = NeuralFoil at the same conditions (the sanity gate). This dataset is the pre-registered holdout: it is shown, but no model constant was tuned on it.
The 6×106 series (squares) crosses the others late in the rise and ends highest at cd 0.0336, M 0.84. The 9×106 series (diamonds) sits ~30 counts high the whole way: trip overdrag, exactly the caveat Harris and McCroskey publish.

3 · ncrit sweep: the tunnel's turbulence level

NeuralFoil free-transition cd vs ncrit; dashed line = the measured plateau (0.0063).
Crossing at ncrit ≈ 4.5. That becomes the convention-table entry for the Langley 8-ft TPT, and with it the free-transition gate passes within 2 counts.

4 · Ferri WR L-143, Fig. 33 — NACA 2309, three sweeps 42 points calibration source, increment-only

Correction from the independent QC pass: two workflow agents re-read this figure with label-anchored programmatic calibration and caught two errors in the first manual read of the diamond curve: a systematic bias of 5–8 counts (glyph tops were read instead of centers) and, above M 0.78, the manual trace had slid onto the neighboring square curve, so the reported "diamond endpoint 0.078" was really the square's. The diamond sweep below is the corrected QC read; the two new sweeps come from the same calibrated pass. This is precisely what the pre-registered double-read rule exists to catch.
Reading the report text corrected its own conditions: Guidonia (Italy) open-jet tunnel, chord 1.575 in, Reynolds number held CONSTANT at 0.34–0.42×106 across all Mach (the documents' "3.4–4.2 million" was a factor-of-ten slip, now fixed everywhere). Green band = NeuralFoil's α = 0 prediction at the true Re band, ncrit 4–9 (cd 0.0062–0.0072). The 1945 data sits 44–54 counts above it at subcritical Mach, so this source enters the study as drag-rise increments only.
Onset order is the first physics win: the measured drag-rise onsets (α = 2° first, then 1°, then 0°) land in exactly the order and location Eq. 8 predicts (Mcrit = 0.630, 0.664, 0.692).

5 · Recalibration pilot: beating the stock pipeline out-of-sample 76% error cut Harris untouched

Corrected 2026-08-23 (second pass, pinned Python path): reading the installed AeroSandbox 4.2.10 source revealed the shipped pipeline is not a pure quartic: past drag divergence (Mcrit+0.068) it switches to a gentler RANS-tuned blend. The first pass compared against the pure quartic extrapolated everywhere, overstating stock's error (574 counts). The table below scores against the exact shipped pipeline, and the whole fit was re-run with scipy soft_l1 in the pinned environment (neuralfoil 0.3.3, aerosandbox 4.2.10). The browser engine reproduced every gate number to all five decimals, so earlier sections stand unchanged.
Selected model (leave-one-sweep-out winner, pinned path, at the true tunnel Reynolds number 0.38×106): ΔCDwave = 1.31 · (M − Mcrit)2.61. Held-out error falls from 258 counts (exact stock pipeline) to 50, and nothing below Mcrit changes by even one count.
All three sweeps collapse onto one curve when plotted against M − Mcrit (each sweep uses its own Eq. 8 Mcrit from the live engine). The stock quartic rockets off the chart; the refit power law tracks the data.
Model (fit on 2 sweeps, scored on the held-out 3rd)◊ held-out□ held-out○ held-outMean MAE
Exact stock pipeline (ASB 4.2.10: quartic to Mdd, RANS blend beyond)155303315258 counts
Null (1 param): k·80(M−Mc)⁴, k ≈ 0.12 (effective constant ~10)78437967 counts
F1 (2 params): A(M−Mc)b, A ≈ 1.31, b ≈ 2.6158335850 counts
No-harm check (the "don't make anything worse" rule): added drag below Mcrit = 0.00 counts on every sweep (structural: the refit term is zero there, so every subcritical prediction, including the two 0.3/0.6-count gate passes, is bit-for-bit unchanged). In the onset window [Mcrit, Mcrit+0.05] the refit is better or equal on all three sweeps: 10.9→10.5, 7.0→4.9, 18.8→18.0 counts. The onset-offset form fit its offset to exactly 0 and was rejected by parsimony.
Side findings. Keeping the stock quartic shape, its constant fits at k·80 ≈ 10, not 80 (the legacy constant 20 is far closer than the shipped value). Engine parity: the pinned Python path reproduced every browser gate number exactly, to all five decimals. Honest scope: this is a pilot on one airfoil from one calibration source (free transition, low Re, M ≤ 0.90 per the frozen Methods); the cross-validation tests generalization across angle of attack, not across airfoils. The full pre-registered Phase B fit decides the paper's constants. The Harris 0012 holdout was not loaded into any fitting code.
